name: Interview plan and scorecard
summary: Before the first interview, the hiring manager and every interviewer share one plan: the criteria the role needs, the same questions in the same order for every candidate, and a blank scorecard each person fills in alone. It rates no one. People make every decision about a candidate.

sources.title: The structure-only rule, the scorecard with no total and evidence written before the rating, criteria taken only from the approved description, the topics-never-raised check, the coverage check, the review notes, the stop conditions, the tests and the worked example.

sources.contribution: Starting from the results a role must produce and deriving the criteria from them; one set of criteria per interview stage, fixed in advance; past-behaviour questions only, at least two per criterion by default, with follow-ups for specifics, and one question on something the candidate owned that failed; a work exercise with feedback and a second attempt, announced in advance; observable behaviours in place of culture fit; independent written ratings before the debrief, least senior speaking first, disagreements first; the hiring manager decides and the debrief does not vote; evidence gaps named; the levels of the default rating scale, which follow the source's evidence standard; and a referred candidate going through the same process as everyone else.
